This page records her sponsorship of the instrument but prints no school library provision.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz.

passages.provision_quote: (2) procedure for each school to allow a: (A) parent or guardian of a student enrolled in the school; or (B) community member: (i) within the school district; or (ii) within the school district in which the charter school is located; to submit a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene (as described in IC 35-49-2-1) or harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); and (3) response and appeal procedure for each school to respond to a removal request submitted by a parent, guardian, or community member described in subdivision (2). (b) The response and appeal procedure established under subsection (a)(3) must require the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting.
passages.note: The enrolled act prints the challenge process but names the governing body as reviewer, not a committee of educators and parents.

rows.reasoning: Donato sponsored HB 1447 (2023) in the Senate and voted Yea on its conference committee report; the act's new school library chapter lets a "parent or guardian" or "community member" request removal of obscene or harmful-to-minors material and requires "the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting." That meets only the first clause of "Remove a challenged book only if a review committee of educators and parents finds it unsuitable" — removal follows a review — because the reviewer named is the school board, not a committee of educators and parents. Rung 4 is excluded too: the act says nothing about access while the request is pending, and the vote itself is on a bill with unrelated parts (Muncie school flexibility, third party vendor surveys, student political activism, criminal code defenses), so it carries direction at most.
